The running head is at the top, the page number at the top right.

main_text.p: Sed quid severiori poetæ Horatio, otium tantopereOd.16. 1.2. commendanti, quid Senecæ Otium Sapientis laudanti,Otium. regerimus? Non est cujusvis, otium recte ferre posse: ut nec benigniorem fortunam: quæ tamen votis nulli fugatur. Otium cum Sapientia exoptandum: qua re-strice[?], ne in lasciviæ scopulos detrudatur, non est exti-mescendum. Otium autem Horatius intelligit vacationem a navigatione lucri causa, a belli gerendi necessitate, ab immoderata honorum ambitione, a cumulandi aurum studio, a peregrinandi inquieto tumultu, a curæ edaci tortura. Negotium quod aut fortunæNegotium. necessitas, aut animi inquietudo impo[?]suit, hoc otio dispungitur.
Non enim gazæ, neque consularis Summovet lictor miseros tumultus Mentis, & curas laqueata circum Tecta volantes.
Vivitur parvo bene, cui paternum Splendet in mensa tenui salinum, Nec leves somnos timor aut cupido Sordidus aufert.

Hoc otium à curâ mentis, & jucunda rerum sublimium contemplatione, non abducit; sed ad eam compendiosa via adducit. Hoc otium ubi nacti fuerimus, non opus erit illo Severi symbolo, Laboremus; aut illo Pertinacis Militemus. Datur enim homini ad altiora nato, præter militiæ durum laborem, honesta vitæ occupatio.
main_text.head: LXXVII.
Pestiferi nomine amicitiæ interimentium morsus.
main_text.p: Nec ulla ratione homine ingenuo digni, aperte enim vel odisse, magis ingenuum est, quam frontem occultare sententiam: ait ille, quid fronte amici afflum-pta interimere? page.notes: Doubtful readings: "Od.16. 1.2." (the chapter number and the "1" could be "l"); "re-strice[?]" at the line break, the word is not clear; "impo[?]suit" is a guess at the letter before "suit", reading "impo-" then "suit" (impo-suit = imposuit). Margin notes "Otium." and "Negotium." are in italics. Long s is transcribed as plain s throughout. Printed hyphens at line ends are kept ("afflum-pta", "exti-mescendum", "cumu-landi", "necef-fitate"). The paragraph break before "Hoc otium" and before "Nec ulla" was judged from the indentation and line ends. The heading "LXXVII." is treated as a bare number, so it is a head at level 1 only because it opens a numbered section; the title below is level 2.
